cursor.note:
THE EVIDENCE MUST CONTAIN THE ASKER. That is the whole of this ticket, and it was found twice at two layers in one night. The retired predicate compared a source's mtime to the mtime in its .pyc header — both terms on disk, and a .pyc is SHARED, so any second interpreter in the same tree repairs the evidence without repairing the asking process. That second actor is not an edge case here; it is CC running proofs and doors in the very tree the daemon watches. Eleven green teeth stood over a live misattribution for exactly as long as no fixture used a real second interpreter.

THEN THE INSTRUMENT TURNED OUT TO HAVE THE PATIENT'S ILLNESS. loop_not_stale took its 'does this folder import cleanly?' reading in its own process, and its own process is the ground loop. It reproduced the stale loop's ImportError and read the misattribution as a real defect. The reading moved to a child seeded from this process's sys.path; two readings over one folder agree on a real defect and disagree on a stale loop.

WHAT THE VERDICT COST, and it is the part worth reading in a year: three of the eight criteria named an instrument that could not have shown what it claimed, and each was replaced rather than reported around. (2) a text grep for 'mtime'/'ImportError' returns 16 and 5 — from the module's own PROSE explaining which face a difference corresponds to, and from the retired comparison deliberately kept as reported-but-not-deciding payload; the instrument that works AST-walks the six deciding functions and asserts the banned spellings are not among the identifiers they touch. (4) reverting the predicate leaves test_discovery GREEN, because the prove-apart pair INJECTS the staleness answer — the deciding branch in loop.py had to be mutated instead (if False: 4 red, if True: 8 red, disjoint). (1) `git stash` cannot make the HEAD-red tooth fail rather than error, because HEAD has no read_all at all. A criterion measured by an instrument that cannot bite is a hollow green, and Law 8 says a false green is worse here than a red.

WHAT DID NOT CLOSE. The standing trouble ground-loop-device-survey is still OPEN, count 1, cleared_by []. A fixed predicate cannot reach an already-benched device — the folder is not even opened while the bench stands, and only TroubleDevice.clear() exits — and the process holding the wrong reading is the one that has to be replaced. It waits on a restart of pid 973171, which is Akien's to perform. This build changes the NEXT misattribution, not this one, and says so rather than letting the trouble look self-clearing.

AND 24% OF HELD OBJECTS READ UNDECIDABLE — 364 of 1497 over 172 modules, against a hypothesis that predicted 'a small, enumerable set'. It costs reach, not correctness (UNDECIDABLE never reads CURRENT), and the honest form of the miss is the number being printed in the coverage tally rather than the adjective being kept in the prose.

The roster rides state() into liveness.json; the armed probe reads that record and clears at ten within-a-beat services under one pid.

SECOND FIX OF THIS CONDITION. The first shipped staleness.py, was cleared 00:51Z by a restart, and was defeated 2h53m later by ordinary work in the same tree. That is why the horizon is 30 days and why the candidate carries no clock and no bytecode: compare what the process HOLDS against a fresh compile of the disk source, which is evidence one of whose terms is the asker.

window.note:
The predicate now holds the asker in it: for every module this process holds whose file is still on disk, the code objects IT HOLDS are compared against a fresh compile of the source — no clock, no .pyc, no error string, no symbol list. Strictly LESS sensitive than the retired mtime comparison (a rewrite with identical content reads fresh) and it answers a question mtime could not answer at all.

Teeth (test_staleness.py, 14, run twice): the deciding one runs a REAL second interpreter, asserts it repaired the .pyc header, and then requires REWRITTEN for both faces — it fails by name against HEAD (AssertionError: []). A second tooth AST-scans the deciding functions and refuses any Name, Attribute or comparison constant naming a symbol, a clock or a bytecode path. A third separates 'compared 398 objects, none disagreed' from 'could compare nothing' — coverage rides the verdict, because findings alone read the same either way. test_discovery gained the tooth that closes the seam this defect lived in: the prove-apart pair INJECTS the staleness answer, so eleven green teeth could not see a blind default; the new one calls the loop with no staleness= at all.

AND THE PROBE WAS FIXED BY THE SAME FINDING. loop_not_stale took its second reading in this process — the suspect — so it reproduced a stale loop's own ImportError and read the misattribution as a real defect. Measured, then moved to a child process seeded from this one's sys.path, through the discovery cache's own probes_for. A refused child is a refusal, never a clean import.

The ticket's watchme now names the built berth and carries a berth_note recording the divergence, so the amendment cannot read as though the cast said this.

WHAT THIS VOYAGE ADDED TO IT, and it came from aiming the finished probe at the world: the second reading — 'does this folder import cleanly?' — was being taken IN THIS PROCESS, and this process is the ground loop, the suspect. A stale loop re-execs the probe file fine and then binds its `from cairn... import` through boot-time sys.modules, so it reproduces the failure and reads a misattributed bench as a real defect. The reading now happens in a child seeded from this process's sys.path, so the only difference between the two readings is what is already held in memory. Two readings over one folder ARE the diagnosis: they agree on a real defect and disagree on a stale loop, and the carry names that pair reproduces_here_but_not_fresh. A refused child is a refusal (fresh_reading_refused), never a clean import — lifting a bench on a dead subprocess would be the loudest version of the same bug.

Armed and verified before this crossing: PROBE.trigger(now, {}) -> True against the live store; watchme_spec_error -> None; armed_error -> None; the berth resolves on disk. The enough clause is spelled by code rather than by prose — it clears only when nothing is wrongly benched AND the store's record of this condition last occurred BEFORE this process started, which is a restart survived rather than a quiet period.

AND THE DEPOSIT IS DURABLE AND UNDELIVERABLE, recorded rather than fixed: the probe fired in the live loop at 04:24:37Z and its carry is in bus_traffic, where 258 rows sit undelivered because harbor_master is pulsed rather than paged. The probe carries no authority (Law 6) — it deposits and pokes — but nothing reads what it deposits, and a ticket is owed for the reader. That is stated here so the watch is not mistaken for a closed loop.
